name: 1634 Prairie Avenue — stone-front house, the north half of the pair with 1636, K01 frontage assembly

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The south-west corner of the K01 footprint, kept from the draft: the rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 30.750, v -3.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.58 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1634 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1634 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced main part s20fp-1634-b1 p2 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft (13.75 m deep, 6.75 m along the front; the part's rectangles cover 86% of its fill). The trace also draws the stone front bay (p1, rectangle u 14.25-15.5, v 0-3.0: the draft's r3), built here as a K08 bay, and the wing behind the rear wall (the draft's r2 and the trace's p3), which is rear_wings (T-2347).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement. The '2B' and the '1' behind it are the rear wing's and its end's (rear_wings).

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a brick (pink) house: the register reads 'brick with stone front'.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft rules' principal floor, 1.4 m over the basement, inside the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8 m; 1628's.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 1628's, inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's starting ranges. The wall head stands at 12.3 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, K02's brown sandstone, smooth-dressed over two rusticated base courses up to the area lights' heads. The sheet says only stone; the brown is chosen on the Prairie library's text record cgn-1634-text (Chicagology's 1634 page), which quotes the Inter Ocean of 10 September 1890 calling the house 'the brown stone mansion No. 1634'. That record is not a source here, so the attribute stays reconstructed. No corner returns: the south corner is the party wall with 1636, and K02 returns the south corner only.

street_front_trim.note: K09 cornice-hood lintels on the two lower storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third, 1628's.

wall_head.note: The bracketed street cornice the register's stone-front family carries: K10's timber brackets and bed moulding under the flat roof's cornice box, along the street front alone (the side walls rise into parapets).

roof_form.note: The stone-front family's flat roof behind its cornice, as the draft rules drew it (k01.roof.flat, from K05's k05.roof.flat_parapet, T-2349): a tin deck falling to the rear wall, a coped parapet on each side wall and a blocking course over the front. No source reads this roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall to the rear fascia, 2 degrees: the K05 variant's own, inside its declared 1-5 degree band.

eave_overhang_m.note: The street cornice box projects 0.6 m from the stone, the brackets' reach with room to the fascia, as 1628's eave.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the pair's north (outer) end, the draft rules' row: 1636 mirrors it to the south.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 6.75 m front, south to north: the stone bay's on the south, and on the north the door with a window a storey over it.

bays.note: The sheet's stone front bay (s20fp-1634-b1 p1, 3.0 m along the front at its south end, 1.25 m out) as K08's rectangular bay, 2.6 m by 1.2 m (the kit's plan, which a record may not resize), three storeys laid in the front's own brownstone (`front_stone`) with a sash to the front and one in each cheek, under a low tin hip that stops under the cornice's brackets (its third storey is 2.1 m to the bay's eave, its sash the K06 ordinary 1.5 m). Its centre is 0.25 m north of the sheet's, to leave K01's 0.3 m pier at the corner.

side_bays.note: None: the south wall is the party wall with 1636 and is built blank.

north_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the north wall, front to rear as K01 reads that wall, one to each room of a three-room-deep house; the wall faces 1630's side yard.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall, north to south. The southern one (s 4.6 m) stands where the rear wing joins (rear_wings, T-2347): on the two lower storeys it is behind the wing and is not cut, the opening into it; on the third, above the wing's deck, it is a window.

rear_wings.note: T-2347: the wing the 1911 sheet draws behind the rear wall, whose PLACE and storey counts are read from the map and whose form is K01's reconstruction. Read on sheet 20 (T-1840 census s20-1634-a1, '2B brick rear wing with a 1-storey end'; trace s20fp-1634-b1 p2 and p3) and measured off the raster through the T-1250 fit, in this frame: (1) REAR_WING, u -6.7 to 0, v 0 to 4.25: the piece lettered '2B', two storeys over a basement, its floors on the main body's first two (1.4 m and 5.4 m) so its string course runs on at the same course. (2) ONE_STOREY_END, u -8.2 to -6.7, v 0 to 4.25: the strip behind a drawn cross wall at the west end, lettered '1' with no 'B', one storey from near grade (floor 0.3 m). The trace's north edge stands at v 4.2-4.3; the draft fitted the wing at u -6.5 to 0 and drew it THREE storeys, its rules' storey count for a wing inside the main part, which the sheet's '2B' corrects. Both pieces stand on the party line with 1636 on the sheet (v -0.7); they are built flush with the main body's south wall at v 0 instead, which K01 fitted 0.7 m inside that line, so the house and its wing keep one south wall (liberty L-k01-1634-stone-front-flat-2350). The south walls are blank party walls, as the main body's. Heights, windows, the flat painted-tin decks, their fascias and 0.15 m overhang are reconstructed: the sheet prints storeys, not heights, and no opening. The two dots the sheet prints in the end are not modelled.

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the principal windows, 0.65 m high so that two rusticated base courses and the coping reach their heads (K02's course range).

roof_covering.note: K04's flat-seam painted tin, the covering of a low-slope deck, with painted tin flashing; no caps, since a flat deck has no hip or ridge.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks against the south party wall, where a rowhouse's flues rise, over the walls between front, middle and back rooms; 0.9 m above the deck's high line. No source reads this house's chimneys.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a straight stoop; the front yard is the draft's street line (24.61 m from the rear corner) less the 13.75 m body.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), stone (blue) front, attached to 1636'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2350 (piece 2 of T-2346) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K02 stone street front, K03 brick side and rear walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 stone front bay, K10 bracketed street cornice — under the flat roof K05 learned for the stone-front rowhouse (T-2349), which K01 now builds as k01.roof.flat. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick with a stone front, attached to 1636, the traced main body and the stone bay before it) through the T-1840 census. Its south wall is the party wall it shares with 1636 and is built blank. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1634-stone-front-flat-2350. T-2347 stands the sheet's '2B' rear wing and its one-storey end behind the rear wall on K01's rear wings (the draft had drawn the wing three storeys by its own rule). No photograph, plate or description of 1634 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
